an7.43:4.1: “Sir, in the morning I robed up and, taking my bowl and robe, entered Kosambī for alms.
an7.43:4.2: Then it occurred to me, sir:
an7.43:4.3: ‘It’s too early to wander for alms in Kosambī.
an7.43:4.4: Why don’t I visit the monastery for the wanderers of other religions?’ …
an7.43:4.6: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, I sat down to one side.
an7.43:5.1: Now at that time, sir, while those wanderers of other religions were sitting together this discussion came up among them:
an7.43:5.2: ‘Reverends, anyone who lives the full and pure spiritual life for twelve years is qualified to be called a graduate mendicant.’
an7.43:5.3: Sir, I neither approved nor rejected that statement of the wanderers of other religions.
an7.43:5.4: Neither approving nor rejecting it, I rose from my seat and left, thinking:
an7.43:5.5: ‘I will learn the meaning of this statement from the Buddha himself.’
